correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, a check with only one erased edge is exactly a known length-two path, so one synchronous round squares the known graph. An induction proves distance threshold 2^t; connected components imply terminal complete multipartite residual and exact sharp round bound. A stopping set is equivalent to the absence of an induced P3 in the known graph, hence uniquely a disjoint-clique partition, giving its Bell polynomial and minimal bipartitions. Fixing vertex-potential y_1=0 proves the F2 kernel dimension n-1 and 2^(c-1) compatible completions. Component-of-vertex decomposition yields the random graph recurrence. Two independent complete row-wise enumerations of all erasure patterns n=3..6, plus a partition/connectedness enumerator through n=7, passed, without treating finite checks as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: An archival practical gap in decoding analysis for a natural universal triangle-check parity system is closed at the full-dynamics level: exact per-round recoverability, fixed-point geometry, all stopping configurations, complete polynomial, sharp worst-round depth, and an exact equivalence of iterative and unique optimal erasure recovery. The theorem is invariant under every relabelling and applies to all n, furnishing reproducible exact finite benchmarks and a transparent link from iterative decoding to graph connectivity; unlike the classical minimum stopping-size bound, the main result controls every initial erasure state.
